note: Each case: steps run in order by tests/dispatch/test_kyd_jobs.py; expect.states is the state sequence each job ends in (every persisted phase, in order; ended:<outcome> last).

cases.name: kt07_three_successive_successful_builds_on_one_slot
cases.why: Each job's claim is released before the slot is used again: claim, release, three times, in that order.

cases.name: kt07_immediate_rework_after_review
cases.why: A registered review is not claim release: while the BUILD job is not closed the slot takes no REWORK; once it is closed the REWORK of the same item opens at once on the same slot and claims again.

cases.name: kt07_blocked_exit
cases.why: A job that exits blocked releases its claim and frees its slot like any other; it is not handled, and its failure class is counted.

cases.name: kt07_restart_after_close_step_result
cases.why: The controller dies right after the close step `result` was persisted. The next controller resumes at the first unfinished step: one `ky release` in all, the slot free only at the end.

cases.name: kt07_restart_after_close_step_exited
cases.why: The controller dies right after the close step `exited` was persisted. The next controller resumes at the first unfinished step: one `ky release` in all, the slot free only at the end.

cases.name: kt07_restart_after_close_step_boundary
cases.why: The controller dies right after the close step `boundary` was persisted. The next controller resumes at the first unfinished step: one `ky release` in all, the slot free only at the end.

cases.name: kt07_restart_after_close_step_claim
cases.why: The controller dies right after the close step `claim` was persisted. The next controller resumes at the first unfinished step: one `ky release` in all, the slot free only at the end.

cases.name: kt07_restart_after_close_step_locks
cases.why: The controller dies right after the close step `locks` was persisted. The next controller resumes at the first unfinished step: one `ky release` in all, the slot free only at the end.

cases.name: lock_resume_never_releases_another_jobs_lock
cases.why: KYDJOBS-R1-B1. The close dies after its locks were released and before the step `locks` was persisted; a REWORK job of the same item takes item.K-1 in the meantime. The resumed close ends the first job and leaves that lock with the job that holds it now, so no VERIFY job can open on the item while the REWORK job holds its worktree.

cases.name: lock_resume_after_a_restart_never_releases_another_jobs_lock
cases.why: KYDJOBS-R1-B1 across a restart: the new controller opens the REWORK job (item.K-1 under its own identity) and then recovers the first job; the resumed close leaves item.K-1 with the REWORK job.

cases.name: kt07_restart_after_close_step_handled
cases.why: The controller dies right after the close step `handled` was persisted. The next controller resumes at the first unfinished step: one `ky release` in all, the slot free only at the end.

cases.name: neg_restart_after_the_release_but_before_it_was_recorded
cases.why: The controller dies after `ky release` succeeded and before the claim step was persisted. The claim file says released for this job's claim_id, so the next controller releases nothing a second time.

cases.name: neg_the_claim_file_claim_id_differs
cases.why: run/claims/b1.json names another claim_id: no `ky release` (it would release whatever that file names), the slot is kept, one owner-wait says reconciliation required. Once the file matches again the close finishes.

cases.name: neg_the_claim_file_item_differs
cases.why: run/claims/b1.json names another item: no `ky release` (it would release whatever that file names), the slot is kept, one owner-wait says reconciliation required. Once the file matches again the close finishes.

cases.name: neg_the_claim_file_worker_differs
cases.why: run/claims/b1.json names another worker: no `ky release` (it would release whatever that file names), the slot is kept, one owner-wait says reconciliation required. Once the file matches again the close finishes.

cases.name: neg_the_claim_file_state_differs
cases.why: run/claims/b1.json is in a state this controller does not know: no `ky release` (it would release whatever that file names), the slot is kept, one owner-wait says reconciliation required. Once the file matches again the close finishes.

cases.name: neg_the_claim_file_is_missing
cases.why: A job that holds a claim_id and finds no claim file cannot show what it would release: nothing is released and the slot is kept.

cases.name: neg_the_release_is_refused_by_the_tracker
cases.why: `ky release` exits non-zero: the claim is not released, the slot is kept, reconciliation required.

cases.name: neg_an_unknown_process_state_is_never_gone_and_never_reaped
cases.why: A start identity that cannot be compared makes the job's state unknown: an owner-wait and nothing else — no timeout kill although the deadline has passed, no renewal, no claim release, the slot kept.

cases.name: neg_a_leader_that_left_members_behind_is_not_gone
cases.why: The leader has exited but its process group still has a member: survivors — an owner-wait only; the group is not signalled and the job is not finished.

cases.name: neg_a_stale_pending_launch_is_never_gone_and_never_relaunched
cases.why: pid "pending" was persisted and the controller died before the start was recorded: whether a process exists is unknown. It is not started again, not recovered as prepared and its claim is not released.

cases.name: timeout_reaps_the_group_sleep
cases.why: Past its deadline the job's group gets TERM, then — still there after the wait — KILL; gone, it is closed timed_out and its claim released.

cases.name: timeout_reaps_the_group_ignore_term
cases.why: Past its deadline the job's group gets TERM, then — still there after the wait — KILL; gone, it is closed timed_out and its claim released.

cases.name: renewal_every_twenty_minutes_and_none_once_termination_begins
cases.why: Only a live job that holds a claim is renewed, and only when the last renewal is 20 minutes old; a job that is terminating is never renewed.

cases.name: recover_a_gone_job
cases.why: Recorded live by an earlier controller and its group gone: interrupted, claim released, re-queued once. The exit code of a process this controller did not start is not known.

cases.name: recover_two_interrupted_jobs_of_one_key_block_it
cases.why: Re-queue once: the second interruption of the same key is not re-queued and blocks automatic attempts; another key of the item is not blocked.

cases.name: recover_a_live_job
cases.why: Recorded live by an earlier controller and still running with its start identity: adopted — supervised by this controller from now on (deadline, renewal), its exit code unknown.

cases.name: recover_an_unknown_job
cases.why: Recorded live by an earlier controller and its state cannot be told: neither interrupted nor adopted — an owner-wait, asked once; the process is not touched.

cases.name: recover_a_prepared_job
cases.why: Prepared by an earlier controller and never started (pid null): closed refused, claim released, slot free.

cases.name: recover_a_terminating_job
cases.why: KYDJOBS-R1-B2. Found terminating by an earlier controller that recorded no outcome: its kind finish never ran, so nothing has checked what the job's own result.json asserts. The plan §6 recovery rule applies: interrupted, the claim released, re-queued once, no handled record; the same key opens again.

cases.name: r2b1_an_unknown_jobs_locks_outlive_its_gone_controller
cases.why: KYDJOBS-R2-B1 case 1. A live job whose state cannot be told; the controller dies and its pid is gone, as a real restart leaves the lock owners. The job's locks name it as their child, so kyaction never takes them over: no REWORK or VERIFY of the item opens into the worktree of a job that may still run, and item.K-1 stays the first job's.

cases.name: r2b1_a_terminating_jobs_locks_outlive_its_gone_controller
cases.why: KYDJOBS-R2-B1 case 2. A close handed a job that still runs (and ignores TERM): terminating, its process live. The controller dies with its pid gone; recover carries the close on, which stops at exited. Its locks are never taken over: no REWORK or VERIFY of the item opens.

cases.name: r2b1_a_stale_pending_launchs_locks_outlive_its_gone_controller
cases.why: KYDJOBS-R2-B1: a start recorded pending, then the controller dies with its pid gone. Whether a process exists is unknown, so its locks are never taken over: no REWORK or VERIFY of the item opens.

cases.name: r2b1_a_gone_jobs_close_releases_the_locks_of_its_gone_controller
cases.why: KYDJOBS-R2-B1, the other side: a lock that names its job is released by that job's own close. The job finished, its controller died with its pid gone; recover closes it interrupted, its locks are released, and a REWORK of the item then opens and holds item.K-1.

cases.name: refusal_after_open_is_closed_refused_and_frees_the_slot
cases.why: The engine refuses a job after open (admission, a failed start): close with outcome refused releases claim and locks; the slot takes the next job; nothing is handled and nothing counted.

cases.name: refusal_by_kyjob_is_refused
cases.why: kyjob.sh refused before any launch and left kyjob.refusal.json: the job is refused, whatever its exit code.

cases.name: quota_refusal_is_fingerprinted_and_not_counted
cases.why: A subscription refusal in the stream gives failure_fp quota: never counted as an attempt, never as an interruption.

cases.name: result_noresult_is_not_a_result
cases.why: A job that ends with no result.json has no result_path; with no outcome handed in it is interrupted, never done.

cases.name: result_otherjob_is_not_a_result
cases.why: A job that ends with a result.json that names another job has no result_path; with no outcome handed in it is interrupted, never done.

cases.name: result_symlink_is_not_a_result
cases.why: A job that ends with a result.json that is a symbolic link has no result_path; with no outcome handed in it is interrupted, never done.

cases.name: open_refuses_a_busy_slot_a_live_key_and_a_handled_key
cases.why: The fresh look under the job lock: a slot or key with a job that has not ended, or a handled key, opens nothing and leaves nothing behind.

cases.name: open_undoes_everything_when_the_claim_is_refused
cases.why: `ky claim` refuses: no job is returned, the locks are free again, the slot takes another item.

cases.name: open_releases_a_claim_whose_answer_was_lost
cases.why: `ky claim` made the claim and its output was lost: the claim id is unknown to the job ("pending"). The claim file shows an active claim of this item by this slot — the job's own — and it is released.

cases.name: open_with_an_unknown_claim_and_no_claim_file_holds_nothing
cases.why: `ky claim` answered nothing usable and no claim file names this item and slot: no claim was made, nothing is released, the slot is free.

cases.name: a_live_job_the_engine_closes_is_stopped_at_its_deadline
cases.why: A close handed a job that still runs stops renewal and waits (the job is not signalled before its deadline); past the deadline the group is reaped like any other, and what it left is read then.

cases.name: a_job_first_seen_gone_by_its_close_is_still_read
cases.why: A close that is the first to see the job gone reads what it left (exit code, session, result event) before anything is released.

cases.name: open_undoes_everything_when_a_lock_is_held
cases.why: The item lock is another job's: nothing is claimed and no job state is written.

cases.name: facts_with_tests_digests_and_migration
cases.why: tests[], test_digests[] and prerequisites[] go into the job state as given; a migration is reserved through kyalloc.py and its first number becomes migration_number, in the state and in the prompt header.

cases.name: facts_without_tests_digests_and_migration
cases.why: Facts that carry none of the three: empty lists, a null migration_number, and kyalloc.py is not run.

cases.name: facts_migration_that_cannot_be_reserved_undoes_the_open
cases.why: kyalloc.py exits 3 (conflicted): no job; the claim is released, the worktree added for it removed.

cases.name: verifier_pool_gets_the_boundary_and_no_claim
cases.why: A verifier-pool job is a boundary verifier and holds no claim: its close releases the boundary view and its job and item locks only. A boundary that cannot be shown released keeps the slot.

cases.name: counts_survive_restart
cases.why: The third identical failure blocks automatic attempts, across a restart and with nothing counted twice when the state write fails between counting and persisting and the close is repeated; a changed evidence fingerprint permits one more attempt; the count is never reset.

cases.name: regen_keeps_its_header_base_sha
cases.why: A launch key in the intent's header overrides the fact of the same name: REGEN keeps its header base_sha; a script job has no slot, no claim and no card, and its job id carries its kind.
